Sourced Statements: Luigi Mangione's New York state murder trial in the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in 2024 has been postponed after he pleaded guilty last week to federal charges and moved to have the state case dismissed, court records show.
Judge Gregory Carro issued a brief order Aug. 17 giving Manhattan prosecutors until Oct. 9 to respond to a defense motion arguing that New York's double jeopardy law bars the state prosecution.
His attorneys argued that the state's double jeopardy law protects him from being prosecuted and punished twice for the same conduct.
State prosecutors have objected to the defense's claim.
Jamie McDonald, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York, said his office would seek the maximum sentence of life in prison.

Sourced Statements: At his plea hearing Aug. 14, Mangione admitted ambushing Thompson outside a Manhattan hotel in December 2024 after planning the attack. He also told the court he 3D-printed a handgun and traveled to New York with the intention of shooting Thompson.
"I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan," Mangione told the judge.
Thompson was shot in early on Dec. 4, 2024, outside a hotel where he was set to speak at an investment conference, authorities said.

Mangione was arrested five days later, on Dec. 9, 2024, in Altoona, Pennsylvania, after an employee and customers at a McDonald's restaurant recognized Mangione from images released by the New York Police Department, authorities said.
Police officials said they matched the gun found in Mangione's possession to casings discovered outside the hotel where Thompson was shot.
Investigators also matched Mangione’s fingerprints to those found on a water bottle and a protein bar wrapper near the scene of the killing, authorities said.
